title: Examples
lead: Eight standalone applications, each covering one decision you make once and live with. Every one of them runs in the browser — Node and the dev server boot inside the tab, with nothing installed locally.

multi-page.title: Multi-page
multi-page.text: Several routes, no locale in the URL. The locale is negotiated per request from a cookie, then Accept-Language.

locale-param.title: Locale in the query
locale-param.text: /about?lang=cs, resolved on the server before rendering. Not the SEO option, and it says so.

locale-router.title: Locale router
locale-router.text: /en/about, /cs/about, /de/about, everything prerendered, with entries() for what the crawler cannot reach.

locale-router-static.title: Static locale router
locale-router-static.text: The same routing with no server at all: one HTML file per page per locale.

locale-router-advanced.title: Advanced locale router
locale-router-advanced.text: The default locale keeps the bare URL and the error page is yours, translated on the first hit. What this site runs on.

component-scoped-csr.title: Component-scoped (CSR)
component-scoped-csr.text: A component carrying its own instance and its own lexicon, loaded in the browser.

component-scoped-ssr.title: Component-scoped (SSR)
component-scoped-ssr.text: The same component, loaded by the page and handed down through snapshot(): complete on the first render.

mdsvex.title: mdsvex
mdsvex.text: A route written in Markdown: t() inside .svx, route-scoped loading, prerendered per locale.
